gateway: isolated temporary home, approval=reads; a freshly seeded gateway for the stub screenshots, one for the live ones and one for the walkthrough; the screenshots taken during the walkthrough (hero, use-case-diagram, use-case-notes, use-case-review) come from the recording's own page in that run, so they show the same run as the video
data: fictional, seeded through the app's HTTP API (capture/scenes.json)

agent_backend.live_model: the operator's own installed, signed-in kiro-cli over ACP with model "auto"; the replies on screen are that model's and vary from run to run
agent_backend.stub: Kiro Crew's offline stub ACP backend (capture/stub_backend.py) for every other scene; no chat reply is shown from it
agent_backend.credit_reading: the browser answers the top bar's credit readout (/api/sessions/usage) with "no reading", so no account balance or email can be shown

speech: the browser ran on Chromium's fake audio device and its speech socket (/api/ws/stt) was answered by capture.py's stand-in, which returns no text of its own; each transcript line is a scripted fictional line the stand-in sent as partial and final frames (the "say" steps in scenes.json), which the page then showed and dispatched to the agents as it does real speech
note: The isolated gateway served this repository's own copy of the app: capture.py's setup installed it from this checkout (POST /api/apps/install), trusted it and enabled it, and every picture shows its committed bundle (ui/dist/index.mjs) and backend. Kiro Crew still ships a built-in meetings app and refuses a second install under the same name, so the Kiro Crew tree the capture ran on is the named commit with only the built-in copy removed (src/kiro_crew/apps/builtins/meetings and its BUILTIN_NAMES row); kirocrew_tree_dirty records that. Its dashboard was built from that same tree (npm ci && npm run build in website/).
data_notes: The meeting, its attendees (Priya, Marco, Dana) and the Lumen mobile app are fictional; every line of the transcript was written for this README.

The capture browser has no microphone and the capture gateway no speech-to-text engine, so the speech socket was answered by capture.py's stand-in: each transcript line is one of the scripted lines (the "say" steps in scenes.json) sent as partial and final recognition frames. The page showed and dispatched each line to the agents exactly as it does real speech.
The notes, the diagram and the action items came from a live model running the app's three agents, so their wording, layout and count differ from run to run.
The meetings on the list page were created through the app's own init, start and stop routes; the dictionary term through its dictionary route.
